study_identification_part.si4_title: Multiscale heterogeneity of functional connectivity in autism

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Use normative modeling to quantify individual-level heterogeneity of functional connectivity (FC) in autism at the levels of connections, regions, and networks, compare overlap patterns between autistic and neurotypical groups, and test associations of FC deviations with clinical and cognitive measures.

rci1_dataset_name.reason: Methods explicitly state pooling from EU-AIMS LEAP and ABIDE I/II.
rci1_dataset_name.supporting_text: We pooled scans from three large datasets: the EU-AIMS Longitudinal European Autism Project (LEAP) ... and the Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchanges I and II, or ABIDE-I and ABIDE-II

rci2_hc_n.supporting_text: The final sample included 796 autistic individuals ... and 1028 neuro-typical (NT) individuals ...

rci3_hc_age.reason: Age range for NT group is given, but no mean/SD are reported in the main text (details likely in Supplement/Table 1).

rci4_hc_sex.reason: Female count reported; male count computed as 1028-256.

rci5_imaging_modality.reason: Methods state resting-state fMRI and structural scans were acquired.
rci5_imaging_modality.supporting_text: Resting-state fMRI and structural scans were obtained using 3T MRI scanners at 32 scanning sites.

rci6_analysis_level.supporting_text: ... examine FC heterogeneity at the level of pair-wise inter-regional connections, specific brain regions, and broader functional networks ...

rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.answer: Schaefer-400 cortical + 15 subcortical ROIs; Pearson correlation of regional time series; Gaussian-gamma mixture normalization; ComBat site-effect regression
rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.reason: Main-text describes parcellation, correlation computation, mixture-model normalization, and ComBat harmonization (software packages for preprocessing are in Supplement).
rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.supporting_text: ... Schaefer parcellation ... 400 ... + 15 subcortical ... Pearson correlations ... normalized ... using Gaussian-gamma mixture modeling ... We used ComBat ... to regress the scan-site-specific effects ...

rci8_quality_checking.supporting_text: Quality control and exclusion criteria are detailed in the Supplement Section 2 and follow previous work (Ilioska et al., 2023).

rci9_site_effect_handling.detail: ComBat harmonization by site on FC matrices; success assessed in Supplement Section 6. Batch variable: scanning site (32 sites).
rci9_site_effect_handling.supporting_text: We used ComBat ... to regress the scan-site-specific effects from the FC data (for a confirmation of the success of this method, see Supplement Section 6).

nm4_response_variable.reason: Parcellation size and edge count are reported; analyses span connection, region, and network levels.
nm4_response_variable.supporting_text: ... 400 functional cortical regions ... + 15 subcortical ... leaving 390 regions ... 75,855 FC estimates ...

nm6_predictor_effects.reason: GPR captures nonlinearities; site handled by batch removal rather than random effects.
nm6_predictor_effects.supporting_text: We used gaussian process regression ... using age, sex, and mean framewise displacement. We used ComBat ... to regress the scan-site-specific effects ...

caa6_deviation_metric.answer: Deviation z-score per edge: (observed - predicted) divided by estimated predictive variance from GPR; extreme deviations thresholded at |Z|>2.3 (p=0.01). Region-level deviation degree and network-level deviation proportion derived thereafter.
caa6_deviation_metric.reason: Computation of deviations and threshold are specified in Methods.
caa6_deviation_metric.supporting_text: Deviations from the normative model were calculated by subtracting the predicted from the observed FC and dividing by the estimated variance ... We applied a threshold of |Z|>2.3 ...

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: SVR with PCA-reduced features to predict clinical/cognitive variables (ADOS, ADI, SRS, SSP, AQ, IQ) from deviation scores at connection, region, and network levels; 5-fold CV with grid search; significance via permutation with FDR correction.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Connection-level FC deviations are highly heterogeneous with minimal overlap; autistic individuals show greater overlap of positive deviations in transmodal systems (DMN, frontoparietal) and negative deviations in sensorimotor areas; deviation patterns predict clinical and cognitive measures.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: No single connection deviated in more than ~3–4% of participants; greater regional and network-level overlap in autism, with positive deviations concentrated within/between DMN and cognitive control networks and negative deviations in somatomotor-related networks. SVR showed significant out-of-sample associations for multiple measures (e.g., SRS, IQ) across levels.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: Normative model trained on NT controls; deviations assessed at multi-scale levels; parcellation: Schaefer-400 + subcortical ROIs; Gaussian-gamma mixture normalization; site harmonization via ComBat; threshold |Z|>2.3; 32 sites across LEAP and ABIDE I/II.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: No fully independent same-domain holdout beyond cross-validation; reliance on ComBat harmonization (potential for residual/over-correction); preprocessing/QC specifics deferred to Supplement; preprint status; modalities limited to resting-state fMRI with parcellation choices potentially influencing results.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: Supplement sections (S1–S10) referenced for dataset details, QC/denoising, ComBat success, calibration metrics, sensitivity analyses. Figures outline overlap analyses and SVR prediction performance.
